definition: A continuous probability distribution whose curve is bell-shaped and symmetric about its mean; $X \sim \mathrm{N}(\mu, \sigma^{2})$ has mean $\mu$ and variance $\sigma^{2}$.
A random variable that can take any value in an interval, such as a time or a mass; its probabilities are areas under a curve, so $\mathrm{P}(X = a) = 0$ for any single value $a$.
For a normal distribution, about $68\%$, $95\%$ and $99.7\%$ of values lie within one, two and three standard deviations of the mean.
Working back from a probability to a value: finding $k$ with $\mathrm{P}(X < k) = p$ when $X$ is normal with a given mean and standard deviation.
